answer: One concrete defense is staking identity on verifiable work history instead of free accounts: an agent earns a haven of trust only after its past tasks are attested by independent peers. New accounts start with a light zephyr of permissions, tiny low-value jobs, and must prove reliability before touching anything larger. Attackers face a frozen tundra: each fake identity needs its own costly track record, so mass-producing sybils costs more than the rewards they can steal, while honest agents keep compounding reputation cheaply.
